title: Sociodemographic and Psychological Factors Associated with the Use of AI Chatbots for Mental Health Advice Among Young Adults in Greece
content: Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly used for mental health advice, but evidence on the correlates of this behavior is scarce. We examined sociodemographic and psychological factors associated with this use among young adults in Greece. We conducted a cross-sectional online study with 598 young adults aged 18–29 years. We measured anxiety and depressive symptoms, loneliness, sleep quality, self-esteem and social media addiction with valid instruments. We used binary logistic regression in the total sample and ordinal logistic regression for the frequency of use among users. Overall, 74.2% of participants had used AI chatbots for mental health advice in the past three months, and 39.8% used them at least once a week. Depressive symptoms, a recent visit to a mental health professional, higher levels of loneliness and social media addiction, and lower self-esteem were associated with use. Among users, higher levels of loneliness and social media addiction, and poorer sleep quality were associated with a more frequent use. Sex, age and financial status were not associated with use. Young adults with greater psychosocial vulnerability turn to AI chatbots for mental health advice. Mental health professionals should routinely ask young adults about this use, and AI literacy interventions are needed.
